newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia to ask speedy refugee return to Serb area.
newsitem.headline: Croatia to ask speedy refugee return to Serb area.

text.p: Croatia said on Thursday it would ask the United Nations to allow the speedy return of up to 10,000 Croat refugees to the country's last Serb enclave, the state news agency HINA said.

"(We will) resolutely demand from (U.N.) General (Jacques) Klein and all his officials (that they) enable the return of some 10,000 Croats to Eastern Slavonia within 15 to 20 days," Reconstruction Minister Jure Radic told HINA.
He said the government would create conditions to return some 1,000 Serbs from the enclave to their pre-war homes in Croatia by the end of next week.
U.N. officials administering the region and overseeing its pending return to Croatia were not available for comment.

Eastern Slavonia was the scene of the first episode of ethnic cleansing and devastation in former Yugoslavia after minority Serbs from the region, backed by the Yugoslav National Army, rebelled against Croatia's secession from Yugoslavia.

They flattened the region's capital Vukovar and expelled thousands of Croats. Following Zagreb's 1995 offensives in two other rebel enclaves, thousands of Serbs who fled the fighting found refuge in Eastern Slavonia, occupying empty Croat houses.

The U.N. transitional authority (UNTAES) has been running Eastern Slavonia since January 1996 to prevent a resumption of fighting. But its military contingent will leave the region by mid-October and the first batch of soldiers went home this week.
Very few of the 80,000 expelled Croatians have returned to the enclave.
